subject: Module ownership matrix + CI blockers for private stack handoff
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Eli Torres <eli@edgeops.io>
Date: 2026-07-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Module ownership matrix + CI blockers for private stack handoff

Team — attaching the initial ownership matrix for the private deployment modules and a short list of CI blockers we've hit during the on-prem dry run. Goal: finalize owners + unblock the CI failures by EOD Wed so the on-prem handoff to AcmeCloud can go ahead on their timeline.

Attachments: owner-matrix.csv, ci-blockers.md

High-level asks:
- Please review the ownership column in owner-matrix.csv and respond with any objections (highlight cells) by EOD Mon.
- Ben / Mina: the CI blockers doc lists two failing acceptance tests (infra/security-group and helm/templates). Ben, can you triage the terraform side? Mina, can you take helm values diffs?
- Eli: Can you confirm the Helm chart compatibility with k8s 1.25 (we saw one failing template render)?

Quick context: Acme wants a VPC/on-prem footprint that mirrors our Dedicated layout: isolated control plane, customer-managed router, and strict CIDR segmentation. The matrix maps module->owner->rollback plan.

Proposed next steps:
- Owners acknowledged in the matrix (Mon EOD)
- CI triage + fixes (target Wed EOD)
- Short sync if blockers persist (30m)

Thanks —
Rishi
Sr. Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Eli Torres <eli@edgeops.io>
Date: 2026-07-05T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Module ownership matrix + CI blockers for private stack handoff

Thanks Rishi — I skimmed the matrix and added a few suggestions in the CSV (comment column). A few notes:
- Control-plane module: prefer to keep ownership with Platform (suggest setting owner to "Platform/infra-team" rather than individual). I'll mark Jonas as primary for now but want Platform as the fallback.
- Networking: we need a clear diagram of the proposed CIDR allocations (private vs customer-managed router). Can someone paste the GIF or link to the diagram in the spreadsheet?

On CI blockers: the helm templates failure looks like a templating guard we added last quarter that assumed cluster-level RBAC exists. Mina — if you can confirm the template change in the patch and add a conditional, that should fix the render.

If we still have failures after fixes, I prefer a quick 20-min call Tue morning (09:30 PT) to avoid slipping Acme's deploy.

—Lauren
Director, Redwood Console

Date: 2026-07-06T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Module ownership matrix + CI blockers for private stack handoff

Rishi / all — quick update from EdgeOps side. I pulled the helm templates against k8s 1.25 and the failing template is due to a values key rename (serviceAccount.create -> serviceAccount.enabled). I attached a small patch that makes the chart tolerant of both keys.

Attachment: helm-values-diff.patch

Also, two questions from Acme:
- Can we provide a minimal rollback procedure for the control-plane helm release? They want explicit steps (helm rollback + how to restore KV state).
- Will the CI pipeline run terraform fmt/tflint as part of PR gating? They've asked for lint checks to be enforced.

I can be on the Tue 09:30 PT call if that helps.

—Eli
EdgeOps — Solutions Engineer
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Eli Torres <eli@edgeops.io>
Date: 2026-07-06T14:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Module ownership matrix + CI blockers for private stack handoff

Quick triage notes for the terraform failures (summary from CI job INF-priv-e2e):
- Failure 1: security-group acceptance test fails — root cause is an ordering race in resource creation for the customer-managed router. Workaround: add explicit depends_on for router attachment in network module.
- Failure 2: tflint rule aws_instance_invalid_type failing on a historical module variant — the CI bundle inspects modules from /modules; we need to drop legacy variants or pin module versioning.

Attachment: ci-failure-logs.txt

Plan: I'll open two PRs today:
1) network: add depends_on + test; owner: ben_carter (me)
2) modules: add module-version gating in CI pipeline (proposed approach: keep semver tags and fail PRs that reference unsupported tags). Owner: jonas_weber to approve gating policy.

Ben
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-07-07T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Module ownership matrix + CI blockers for private stack handoff — action items

Thanks everyone — good progress. Consolidating action items here so we can close the loop before the handoff: 

1) owner-matrix.csv: owners confirmed except Platform fallback change (Lauren/Jonas) — Rishi to update sheet by Mon.
2) helm templates: Eli + Mina to merge helm-values-diff.patch and add conditional handling for both keys (target: Tue AM). Owner: mina_haddad.
3) terraform/network race: Ben to push depends_on fix and attach a test (target: Tue EOD). Owner: ben_carter.
4) CI gating: Jonas to draft module-version gating policy and add tflint/tfsec steps to PR pipeline (target: Wed). Owner: jonas_weber.
5) Rollback doc: Rishi to draft minimal rollback procedure and post to the INF Jira.

Related links: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1245 (rollback doc + test cases)

If all items land by Wed EOD, we keep Acme's handoff slot on Thu. If any of the gating changes cascade, we will push and notify Acme immediately.

Thanks —
Rishi
Sr. Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
